12.4: Explicitly apportions the lamb according to each person’s eating, rather than leaving this as “accordingly.”
12.5: Retains the age expression “a son of a year.”
12.6: “Slaughter it” has a singular object rather than “slaughter the animals”; the time is “between the two evenings.”
12.7: Names the two doorposts and the lintel, rather than the sides and tops of doorframes.
12.10: What remains until morning is to be burned with fire; the wording does not add “before the morning.”
12.11: “Your loins girded” retains the bodily image rather than “fully dressed for travel.”
12.12: Says “every firstborn,” without a separate adjective “male.”
12.13: The blood is “a sign for you,” rather than simply distinguishing the houses.
12.14: Repeats the command to celebrate the day after describing the perpetual statute.
12.16: The exception is expressed as “that which is eaten by every person,” rather than explicitly “prepare the meals.”
12.17: Says to keep the unleavened bread, without an explicit word “Feast.”
12.21: Retains the two actions “draw out and take,” rather than “Go at once and select.”
12.22: Repeats “the blood which is in the basin” and explicitly names the lintel and two doorposts.
12.23: Names the LORD again as the subject of passing over the doorway, rather than continuing only with pronouns.
12.24: Names “your sons,” rather than the broader “your descendants.”
12.27: Retains the two bodily actions of bowing low and prostrating themselves, rather than describing the second only as worship.
12.28: Repeats “they did” after naming what the LORD commanded Moses and Aaron.
12.29: “The house of the pit” retains the compound image rendered “the dungeon”; no separate adjective “male” is added to the firstborn.
12.30: Calls Pharaoh’s attendants his servants rather than his officials.
12.31: “Serve the LORD” retains the service verb rendered “worship the LORD.”
12.33: Does not explicitly add “otherwise” to the Egyptians’ explanation.
12.37: Names “the little ones,” without a separate noun “women.”
12.42: “A night of watchings for the LORD” does not explicitly make the LORD the subject of keeping a vigil.
12.44: Names money as the means of purchase, rather than simply saying the slave was purchased.
12.46: Retains the singular “a bone,” rather than “any of the bones.”
12.48: Does not explicitly insert “wants” before the foreigner’s observance of the Passover.

13.2: Retains the opening of every womb, without a separate adjective “male” in this verse.
13.3: “The house of slaves” retains the plural people noun rather than the abstract “house of slavery.”
13.7: The prohibition says leaven is not to be seen, rather than merely not to be found.
13.9: Places the reminder “between your eyes,” rather than on the forehead, and the law “in your mouth,” rather than on the lips.
13.10: “From days to days” retains the repeated day expression rendered “year after year.”
13.11: Retains the singular collective designation “the Canaanite,” rather than the plural “the Canaanites.”
13.14: The son’s question is “What is this?” rather than the expanded “What does this mean?”
13.16: Places the marks “between your eyes,” rather than on the forehead.
13.17: Describes the road as “near,” rather than using the comparative “shorter.”
13.18: “Sea of Reeds” retains the reed noun rendered “Red Sea.”
13.19: The promise uses “visit,” rather than “attend to.”
13.21: Retains “by day and night,” rather than “by day or night.”

14.4: “Make strong” retains the verb applied to Pharaoh’s heart rather than “harden.”
14.5: The heart of Pharaoh and his servants is turned, retaining the heart image and passive wording rather than their changing their minds.
14.6: Says Pharaoh harnessed his chariot and took his people, rather than merely prepared the chariot and took his army.
14.7: Calls the six hundred chariots chosen, rather than the best, and does not explicitly add “other” before all the chariots of Egypt.
14.8: “With a raised hand” retains the bodily image rendered “defiantly.”
14.9: Speaks of Pharaoh’s chariot horses rather than listing horses and chariots as separate items.
14.10: Retains “lifted their eyes” and repeats the Israelites as the subject of crying out.
14.13: “See” is an imperative rather than the prediction “you will see.”
14.14: Does not explicitly add “only” to the instruction to keep silent.
14.17: The heart of Egypt is singular rather than “the hearts of the Egyptians.”
14.20: Joins the cloud and darkness with “and”; the lighting of the night is also joined by “and,” rather than “but.”
14.21: Keeps the LORD as the subject of making the sea dry, rather than the wind as subject of a relative clause.
14.22: The predicate “a wall” is singular rather than “walls of water.”
14.24: Repeats the Egyptian camp rather than switching from “army” to “camp.”
14.25: Uses a removal verb for the chariot wheels rather than saying they wobbled.
14.27: Retains their fleeing “to meet it” and the image of the LORD shaking the Egyptians, rather than simply their retreating and being swept into the sea.
14.29: The predicate “a wall” is singular rather than “walls of water.”
14.31: “The great hand” retains the bodily image rendered “great power.” The LORD is named again as the object of belief rather than replaced by “Him.”

27.1: The altar is definite, “the altar,” rather than “an altar.”
27.4: Names four bronze rings at the four extremities, rather than expressing the number as one ring at each corner.
27.8: Ends with the plural active “they will make it,” rather than an impersonal passive.
27.14: Retains the shoulder term used for the side of the entrance.
27.15: “The second side” preserves the ordinal rather than “the other side.”
27.16: Describes a screen of twenty cubits for the gate, rather than making the gate itself the grammatical subject of the measurement.
27.18: Repeats “fifty” in the width specification; BSB states it once.
27.20: The lamp is singular rather than the plural “lamps.”
27.21: The object being tended is singular “it,” rather than the plural “the lamps.”

28.1: Priestly service is expressed in the singular rather than “as priests.”
28.3: Describes the craftsmen as “wise of heart,” retaining the heart image rather than simply “skilled craftsmen.”
28.4: The final priestly service phrase is singular rather than “they may serve Me as priests.”
28.5: Uses “take” for the materials rather than “use.”
28.6: Calls it the work of a skilled designer rather than specifying embroidery.
28.7: Names two ends rather than two corners.
28.10: “The second stone” retains the ordinal rather than “the other.”
28.15: Repeats the making instruction three times: for the breastpiece, its correspondence to the ephod, and its materials.
28.23: Names the two ends of the breastpiece rather than two corners.
28.24: Names the ends of the breastpiece rather than the corners.
28.25: Retains “the two ends of the two cords,” without explicitly adding “other.”
28.26: Does not explicitly add “more” to the rings or “other” to the ends.
28.27: Does not explicitly add “additional” to the rings.
28.28: People bind the breastpiece by its rings; the breastpiece remains the object rather than making its rings the subject of a passive clause.
28.32: Uses mouth and lip imagery for the opening and its border.
28.33: Repeats the hem and the phrase “all around,” rather than compressing them to a single description.
28.34: Repeats “a gold bell and a pomegranate” twice rather than summarizing them as alternating plural objects.
28.35: The coming in and going out are joined by “and” rather than “or.”
28.40: Repeats the making instruction for the tunics, sashes, and headdresses rather than using one verb for the list.
28.41: “Fill their hand” retains the hand image rendered “ordain them.”
28.43: “His seed after him” retains the seed image and the following relation rather than simply “his descendants.”

39.2: The Hebrew says “he made,” without naming the maker here; BSB supplies “Bezalel.”
39.3: The Hebrew changes from plural “they hammered” to singular “he cut”; BSB uses “they” for both actions. The Hebrew also repeats “in among” for the four materials.
39.4: The Hebrew calls the joining points “its two ends”; BSB calls them “its two corners.”
39.7: The Hebrew says “he put” the stones on the shoulder pieces; BSB says “they fastened” them.
39.9: The Hebrew states “folded double” twice and includes “they made the breastpiece”; BSB gives the folding description once and omits that separate making clause.
39.16: The Hebrew says “the two ends of the breastpiece”; BSB says “the two corners of the breastpiece.”
39.17: The Hebrew says “the two ends of the breastpiece”; BSB says “the two corners of the breastpiece.”
39.18: The Hebrew says “the two ends of the two cords”; BSB adds “other” in “the other ends of the two chains.”
39.19: The Hebrew says “two gold rings” and “the two ends”; BSB says “two more gold rings” and “the other two corners.”
39.20: The Hebrew says “two gold rings”; BSB adds “additional.”
39.21: The Hebrew makes the breastpiece the object of “they bound,” with its rings connecting it to the ephod’s rings; BSB makes the rings themselves the object of “they tied.”
39.22: The Hebrew says “he made” the robe; BSB says “they made” it.
39.23: The Hebrew describes the opening as a “mouth” and its edging as a “lip”; BSB uses “opening” and “collar.”
39.24: The Hebrew lists blue, purple, and scarlet, followed by “twisted”; it does not explicitly name linen here. BSB adds “and finely spun linen.”
39.25: The Hebrew repeats “between the pomegranates” twice; BSB expresses the placement once.
39.26: The Hebrew repeats “a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate”; BSB condenses this to “alternating bells and pomegranates.”
39.30: The Hebrew says they “wrote on it a writing,” followed by a description of seal engravings; BSB expresses the action as engraving an inscription.
39.31: The Hebrew explicitly places the plate on the turban “above”; BSB omits that positional word.
39.32: The Hebrew repeats the doing clause, ending “so they did”; BSB states the Israelites’ obedience once.
39.37: The Hebrew says “the pure lampstand,” without explicitly naming gold in this verse. BSB adds “gold” and combines “its lamps, the lamps of the arrangement” into “its row of lamps.”
39.43: The Hebrew includes “and behold” and repeats “they did” in its account of the work; BSB condenses these into the statement that they had accomplished it.

40.1: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
40.10: The Hebrew repeats “the altar” in the final clause and calls it “holiness of holinesses”; BSB uses “it” and “most holy.”
40.11: The Hebrew ends “consecrate it,” with a singular object; BSB says “consecrate them.”
40.16: The Hebrew repeats the action, ending “so he did”; BSB expresses Moses’ obedience once.
40.19: The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
40.20: The Hebrew uses an unnamed “he” and says he put the poles “on the ark”; BSB names Moses and describes the poles as being attached to it.
40.21: The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
40.22: The Hebrew has an unnamed “he” and uses the body image “thigh” for the tabernacle’s side; BSB names Moses and says “side.”
40.23: The Hebrew says he “arranged an arrangement of bread” and ends with Moses’ name; BSB reduces the repeated arrangement wording and uses “him.”
40.24: The Hebrew uses the body image “thigh” for the tabernacle’s side; BSB says “side” and adds “also.”
40.25: The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
40.26: The Hebrew says “he placed”; BSB supplies the name Moses.
40.27: The Hebrew ends “as the LORD commanded Moses”; BSB replaces the repeated name with “him.”
40.29: The Hebrew places the altar “at the entrance” and ends with Moses’ name; BSB says “near the entrance” and replaces the name with “him.”
40.32: The Hebrew links entering the tent and approaching the altar with “and”; BSB uses “or.”
